------------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m8p1t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Stations, Budget, NONE
VARIABLES coarse, fine, record, remaining, local, phase

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Stations \cup {NONE}
    /\ fine \in Stations \cup {NONE}
    /\ record \in 0..Budget
    /\ remaining \in 0..Budget
    /\ local \in [Stations -> 0..Budget]
    /\ phase \in [Stations -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine", "wrote"}]

Init ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ fine = NONE
    /\ record = 0
    /\ remaining = Budget
    /\ local = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [s \in Stations |-> "idle"]

AcquireCoarse(s) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "idle"
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ coarse' = s
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "coarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, record, remaining, local>>

AcquireFine(s) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "coarse"
    /\ coarse = s
    /\ fine = NONE
    /\ fine' = s
    /\ local' = [local EXCEPT ![s] = record]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "fine"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, record, remaining>>

Commit(s) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "fine"
    /\ fine = s
    /\ remaining > 0
    /\ record' = 1 + record
    /\ remaining' = remaining - 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "wrote"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, local>>

Release(s) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "wrote"
    /\ coarse' = NONE
    /\ fine' = NONE
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, remaining, local>>

Abort(s) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "fine"
    /\ fine = s
    /\ remaining = 0
    /\ coarse' = NONE
    /\ fine' = NONE
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, remaining, local>>

Next == \E s \in Stations : AcquireCoarse(s) \/ AcquireFine(s) \/ Commit(s) \/ Release(s) \/ Abort(s)

vars == <<coarse, fine, record, remaining, local, phase>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == \A s \in Stations : (fine = s /\ phase[s] = "fine") => local[s] = record
Conservation == record = Budget - remaining
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Stations = {s1, s2}
CONSTANT Budget = 3
CONSTANT NONE = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
INVARIANT Conservation
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash stations that all update one shared throughput record. To touch the record a station must first take a coarse line-level lock and then, underneath it, a fine record-level lock; it reads the record's current value into a local scratch copy, adds its own tally, and writes the sum back. Grant and release requests travel over the plant network and may be delivered to the controller in any order, so the controller must be safe under arbitrary interleaving. The hierarchy exists so that no two stations can be midway through a read-modify-write on the record at the same time, which would silently drop one station's update. A station that holds the fine lock must be sure the value it read is still the record's current value before it commits its write. Only after writing does a station release both locks and return to idle. The record starts at zero with every station idle and no locks held.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a station holds the fine record-level lock, the value it snapshotted still equals the live record, so no concurrent update can have been lost between its read and its write.

EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Offices, Seats, MaxTerm

VARIABLES yes, term, officeTerm, drawn, seats, offline

Init ==
    /\ yes = {}
    /\ term = 0
    /\ officeTerm = [o \in Offices |-> 0]
    /\ drawn = 0
    /\ seats = Seats
    /\ offline = 0

CastYes(o) ==
    /\ o \notin yes
    /\ officeTerm[o] = term
    /\ yes' = yes \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, officeTerm, drawn, seats, offline>>

CommitEnrollment ==
    /\ yes = Offices
    /\ seats > 0
    /\ drawn' = 1 + drawn
    /\ seats' = seats - 1
    /\ yes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, officeTerm, offline>>

StudentDrop ==
    /\ drawn > 0
    /\ drawn' = drawn - 1
    /\ seats' = seats + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yes, term, officeTerm, offline>>

AdvanceTerm ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ yes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<officeTerm, drawn, seats, offline>>

RefreshOffice(o) ==
    /\ officeTerm[o] < term
    /\ officeTerm' = [officeTerm EXCEPT ![o] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yes, term, drawn, seats, offline>>

RetireSeat ==
    /\ seats > 0
    /\ seats' = seats - 1
    /\ offline' = offline + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yes, term, officeTerm, drawn>>

ReinstateSeat ==
    /\ offline > 0
    /\ offline' = offline - 1
    /\ seats' = seats + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yes, term, officeTerm, drawn>>

Next ==
    \/ CommitEnrollment \/ StudentDrop \/ AdvanceTerm \/ RetireSeat \/ ReinstateSeat
    \/ \E o \in Offices : CastYes(o) \/ RefreshOffice(o)

NoStaleVote == \A o \in yes : officeTerm[o] = term
SeatAccounting == drawn = Seats - seats - offline

TypeOK ==
    /\ yes \subseteq Offices
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ officeTerm \in [Offices -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ drawn \in 0..Seats
    /\ seats \in 0..Seats
    /\ offline \in 0..Seats

CONSTANT Seats = 3
CONSTANT MaxTerm = 2

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleVote
INVARIANT SeatAccounting
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
A university course-registration system confirms each enrollment through a two-phase agreement between the registrar and the departmental offices. Every office casts a yes-vote stamped with the registration term it believes is current, and only when every office holds a live yes-vote may the registrar commit an enrollment, which draws one seat from the course's seat pool. The registrar periodically advances the registration term, which voids all outstanding votes, and an office that has not refreshed to the current term is stale: a stale office's vote must never stand. Capacity changes at runtime: the dean may retire an unused seat from the pool for maintenance and later reinstate it, so the live pool grows and shrinks while rounds are in progress. Students may also drop a confirmed enrollment, returning its seat to the pool. Offices refresh themselves by adopting the current term. The system starts with no votes, an empty retired set, a full pool, and every office on the current term.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no enrollment commit ever counts a yes-vote from an office whose term stamp is older than the registrar's current registration term.

EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Ring, TraySlots, MaxJobs

VARIABLES token, transit, rack, printed, submitted

Init ==
    /\ token \in Ring
    /\ transit = {}
    /\ rack = <<>>
    /\ printed = 0
    /\ submitted = 0

PassToken ==
    /\ \E w \in Ring : w /= token /\ token' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED <<transit, rack, printed, submitted>>

SubmitJob(w) ==
    /\ token = w
    /\ submitted < MaxJobs
    /\ submitted' = submitted + 1
    /\ transit' = transit \cup {submitted}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, rack, printed>>

RackArrival(j) ==
    /\ j \in transit
    /\ Len(rack) < TraySlots
    /\ rack' = Append(rack, j)
    /\ transit' = transit \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed, submitted>>

PressJob ==
    /\ Len(rack) > 0
    /\ printed' = 1 + printed
    /\ rack' = Tail(rack)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, transit, submitted>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken \/ PressJob
    \/ \E w \in Ring : SubmitJob(w)
    \/ \E j \in transit : RackArrival(j)

vars == <<token, transit, rack, printed, submitted>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RackWithinSlots == Len(rack) <= TraySlots
JobAccounting == printed = submitted - Len(rack) - Cardinality(transit)

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Ring
    /\ transit \subseteq 0..MaxJobs
    /\ rack \in Seq(0..MaxJobs)
    /\ printed \in 0..MaxJobs
    /\ submitted \in 0..MaxJobs
===========================================================================

CONSTANT TraySlots = 2
CONSTANT MaxJobs = 4

INVARIANT RackWithinSlots
INVARIANT JobAccounting
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
A print shop runs a job spooler fed by a ring of workstations. A single permission token circulates around the ring, and only the workstation currently holding the token may submit a print job. Submitted jobs travel over the shop network to the spooler, and the network can deliver them in any order, so a job sent first may arrive last. The spooler holds arriving jobs in a rack of trays with a fixed number of slots, and it refuses to accept an arriving job when every tray is occupied, leaving the job in transit until space opens. The press takes the oldest job from the rack, prints it, and frees its tray. The token itself simply passes from one workstation to the next around the ring at any time. Each job is numbered when submitted, so the shop can always account for every job as either in transit, racked, or printed. Initially no jobs exist, the rack is empty, and the first workstation holds the token.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of jobs held in the spooler's rack never exceeds the fixed number of tray slots.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m4p2t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Robots, OrderIds, Totes, QCap

VARIABLES shelf, gripping, docked, workq, radio

Carried == Cardinality({r \in Robots : gripping[r]})

Init ==
    /\ shelf = Totes
    /\ gripping = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
    /\ docked = 0
    /\ workq = <<>>
    /\ radio = {}

InQueue(id) == \E i \in 1..Len(workq) : workq[i] = id

IssueOrder(id) ==
    /\ id \notin radio
    /\ ~InQueue(id)
    /\ radio' = radio \cup {id}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, gripping, docked, workq>>

DeliverOrder(id) ==
    /\ id \in radio
    /\ Len(workq) < QCap
    /\ workq' = Append(workq, id)
    /\ radio' = radio \ {id}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, gripping, docked>>

GrabTote(r) ==
    /\ ~gripping[r]
    /\ Len(workq) > 0
    /\ shelf > 0
    /\ gripping' = [gripping EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ shelf' = shelf - 1
    /\ workq' = Tail(workq)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<docked, radio>>

DropAtDock(r) ==
    /\ gripping[r]
    /\ docked' = 1 + docked
    /\ gripping' = [gripping EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, workq, radio>>

Restock ==
    /\ docked > 0
    /\ docked' = docked - 1
    /\ shelf' = shelf + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gripping, workq, radio>>

Next ==
    \/ Restock
    \/ \E id \in OrderIds : IssueOrder(id) \/ DeliverOrder(id)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : GrabTote(r) \/ DropAtDock(r)

vars == <<shelf, gripping, docked, workq, radio>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ToteConservation == docked = Totes - shelf - Carried
QueueBackpressure == Len(workq) <= QCap

TypeOK ==
    /\ shelf \in 0..Totes
    /\ gripping \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ docked \in 0..Totes
    /\ workq \in Seq(OrderIds)
    /\ radio \subseteq OrderIds
===========================================================================

CONSTANT Robots = {r1, r2}
CONSTANT OrderIds = {o1, o2, o3}
CONSTANT Totes = 3
CONSTANT QCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ToteConservation
INVARIANT QueueBackpressure
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet moves totes from a storage shelf to a shipping dock under the direction of a central dispatcher. The dispatcher issues numbered move orders that travel over the warehouse radio network, and the network may deliver them in any order, so orders do not arrive in the sequence they were issued. Arriving orders land in a bounded work queue in front of the robots; when the queue is full the network holds the order back, applying backpressure until a slot frees up. An idle robot takes the order at the head of the queue, lifts one tote off the shelf, and carries it across the floor. When the robot reaches the dock it sets the tote down, completing the order and freeing itself for new work. Dock workers periodically restock delivered totes back onto the shelf, so totes circulate through the system endlessly. Every tote is always in exactly one place: on the shelf, in a robot's grip, or on the dock, and none are ever created or destroyed. Initially all totes sit on the shelf, the queue and the radio network are empty, and every robot is idle.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the totes on the shelf, in robots' grips, and on the dock always add up to the fleet's fixed tote population, with none created or destroyed.

EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS RingEq, RingFu, Credits, IDLE

Gateways == RingEq \cup RingFu

VARIABLES tokEq, tokFu, engine, stage, settled, credits

Init ==
    /\ tokEq \in RingEq
    /\ tokFu \in RingFu
    /\ engine = IDLE
    /\ stage = [g \in Gateways |-> "waiting"]
    /\ settled = 0
    /\ credits = Credits

RotateEq ==
    /\ \E g \in RingEq : g /= tokEq /\ tokEq' = g
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokFu, engine, stage, settled, credits>>

RotateFu ==
    /\ \E g \in RingFu : g /= tokFu /\ tokFu' = g
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokEq, engine, stage, settled, credits>>

HoldsOwnToken(g) == \/ (g \in RingEq /\ tokEq = g)
                    \/ (g \in RingFu /\ tokFu = g)

EnterEngine(g) ==

    /\ engine = IDLE
    /\ credits > 0
    /\ engine' = g
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![g] = "crossing"]
    /\ credits' = credits - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokEq, tokFu, settled>>

LeaveEngine(g) ==
    /\ stage[g] = "crossing"
    /\ engine' = IDLE
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![g] = "waiting"]
    /\ settled' = 1 + settled
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokEq, tokFu, credits>>

    \/ RotateEq \/ RotateFu
    \/ \E g \in Gateways : EnterEngine(g) \/ LeaveEngine(g)

    /\ tokFu \in RingFu
    /\ engine \in Gateways \cup {IDLE}
    /\ stage \in [Gateways -> {"waiting", "crossing"}]
    /\ settled \in 0..Credits
    /\ credits \in 0..Credits

INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction with two independent order books, one for equities and one for funds, that share a single crossing engine and a single pool of crossing credits. Each book has its own ring of gateway servers, and a permission token circulates independently around each ring. A gateway may step into the shared crossing engine only when it holds its own book's token, the engine is unoccupied, and a crossing credit remains in the shared pool; stepping in consumes one credit. While a gateway occupies the engine it computes the opening cross for its book, then steps out, recording one settled cross. Credits are never returned, so the pool only drains as crosses complete, and both books draw from the same pool. Tokens keep circulating around their rings regardless of what the engine is doing. The auction starts with the engine empty, the credit pool full, no settled crosses, and one gateway in each ring holding its token.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one gateway ever occupies the shared crossing engine at a time, and every gateway that believes it is crossing is the one the engine records.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m9p0t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cars, Orders, MaxEpoch, FREE

VARIABLES epoch, grantee, grantEp, duty, backlog, serviced

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ grantee = FREE
    /\ grantEp = 0
    /\ duty = [c \in Cars |-> "idle"]
    /\ backlog = Orders
    /\ serviced = 0

GrantBay(c) ==
    /\ grantee = FREE
    /\ duty[c] = "idle"
    /\ backlog > 0
    /\ grantee' = c
    /\ grantEp' = epoch
    /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![c] = "bay"]
    /\ backlog' = backlog - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, serviced>>

FinishService(c) ==
    /\ duty[c] = "bay"
    /\ grantee = c
    /\ grantEp = epoch
    /\ serviced' = 1 + serviced
    /\ grantee' = FREE
    /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantEp, backlog>>

CrashSilently(c) ==
    /\ duty[c] /= "dead"
    /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![c] = "dead"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee, grantEp, backlog, serviced>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ grantee /= FREE
    /\ duty[grantee] = "dead"
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ grantee' = FREE
    /\ backlog' = backlog + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grantEp, duty, serviced>>

Repair(c) ==
    /\ duty[c] = "dead"
    /\ grantee /= c
    /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee, grantEp, backlog, serviced>>

Next == \E c \in Cars :
    GrantBay(c) \/ FinishService(c) \/ CrashSilently(c) \/ Repair(c) \/ Reconfigure

vars == <<epoch, grantee, grantEp, duty, backlog, serviced>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BayMutex == \A c \in Cars : duty[c] = "bay" => (grantee = c /\ grantEp <= epoch)
OrderLedger == serviced = Orders - backlog - (IF grantee = FREE THEN 0 ELSE 1)

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ grantee \in Cars \cup {FREE}
    /\ grantEp \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ duty \in [Cars -> {"idle", "bay", "dead"}]
    /\ backlog \in 0..Orders
    /\ serviced \in 0..Orders
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Cars = {c1, c2}
CONSTANT Orders = 3
CONSTANT MaxEpoch = 2
CONSTANT FREE = FREE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BayMutex
INVARIANT OrderLedger
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper shares a single maintenance bay where one car at a time can be serviced. A bank controller hands out bay grants stamped with the current configuration epoch, drawing one work order from its backlog for each grant. The car holding a current-epoch grant occupies the bay, finishes its service, and returns the grant, marking the order serviced. Any car can crash silently at any moment, even while occupying the bay, and it gives no notification. When the controller observes that the grant holder has gone dead, it reconfigures: it advances the epoch, revokes the stale grant, and returns the unfinished work order to the backlog. Grants stamped with an old epoch are void, so a revoked car can never be counted as occupying the bay. Maintenance crews repair dead cars that do not hold the grant, returning them to idle duty. Initially the backlog is full, no car holds a grant, and every car is idle.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one elevator car ever occupies the maintenance bay, and any occupying car holds the controller's grant stamped with the current epoch.

EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Terminals, Copies, MaxLap

VARIABLES holder, lap, session, reserved, pool

Init ==
    /\ holder \in Terminals
    /\ lap = 0
    /\ session = [t \in Terminals |-> 0]
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ pool = Copies

PassToken ==
    /\ lap < MaxLap
    /\ \E t \in Terminals : t /= holder /\ holder' = t
    /\ lap' = lap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, reserved, pool>>

OpenSession(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ session[t] < lap \/ lap = 0
    /\ session' = [session EXCEPT ![t] = lap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, lap, reserved, pool>>

ReserveCopy(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ session[t] = lap
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ reserved' = 1 + reserved
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, lap, session>>

LibrarianOverride ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ reserved' = 1 + reserved
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, lap, session>>

PatronReturn ==
    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, lap, session>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken \/ LibrarianOverride \/ PatronReturn
    \/ \E t \in Terminals : OpenSession(t) \/ ReserveCopy(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleSession ==
    \A t \in Terminals : (session[t] = lap /\ lap > 0) => holder = t
CopyLedger == reserved = Copies - pool

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Terminals
    /\ lap \in 0..MaxLap
    /\ session \in [Terminals -> 0..MaxLap]
    /\ reserved \in 0..Copies
    /\ pool \in 0..Copies

INVARIANT CopyLedger

nl:
A library book reservation system connects the branch terminals in a logical ring around which a single authorization token travels. Each pass of the token starts a new lap, and a terminal may open a reservation session only while it actually holds the token; the session is stamped with the lap number at which it was opened. When the token moves on, the lap number advances and every previously opened session becomes stale, so a terminal that still believes it is authorized from an earlier lap must be refused. A terminal with a live current-lap session may reserve a copy of a book, taking one copy from the branch pool. A privileged head librarian can override the ring entirely and place a reservation without any token, which also draws from the same pool. Patrons return reserved copies to the pool over time, so copies circulate. Initially the pool is full, no reservations exist, no sessions are open, and the first terminal holds the token on lap zero.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no terminal ever holds a reservation session stamped as current while the authorization token is at another terminal, so no stale or unauthorized terminal can place a reservation.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m0p1t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Pharmacists, Stock, MaxVer

VARIABLES ver, stock, dispensed, snapVer, snapStock, shift

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ stock = Stock
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ snapVer = [p \in Pharmacists |-> 0]
    /\ snapStock = [p \in Pharmacists |-> Stock]
    /\ shift = [p \in Pharmacists |-> "idle"]

ReadLedger(p) ==
    /\ shift[p] = "idle"
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![p] = ver]
    /\ snapStock' = [snapStock EXCEPT ![p] = stock]
    /\ shift' = [shift EXCEPT ![p] = "preparing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, stock, dispensed>>

CommitDispense(p) ==
    /\ shift[p] = "preparing"
    /\ snapVer[p] = ver
    /\ stock > 0
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ dispensed' = 1 + dispensed
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ shift' = [shift EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVer, snapStock>>

RetryStale(p) ==
    /\ shift[p] = "preparing"
    /\ shift' = [shift EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, stock, dispensed, snapVer, snapStock>>

CrashSilently(p) ==
    /\ shift[p] /= "down"
    /\ shift' = [shift EXCEPT ![p] = "down"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, stock, dispensed, snapVer, snapStock>>

BackOnShift(p) ==
    /\ shift[p] = "down"
    /\ shift' = [shift EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, stock, dispensed, snapVer, snapStock>>

Next == \E p \in Pharmacists :
    ReadLedger(p) \/ CommitDispense(p) \/ RetryStale(p)
    \/ CrashSilently(p) \/ BackOnShift(p)

vars == <<ver, stock, dispensed, snapVer, snapStock, shift>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FreshSnapshotAgrees ==
    \A p \in Pharmacists :
        (shift[p] = "preparing" /\ snapVer[p] = ver) => snapStock[p] = stock
StockLedger == dispensed = Stock - stock

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ stock \in 0..Stock
    /\ dispensed \in 0..Stock
    /\ snapVer \in [Pharmacists -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ snapStock \in [Pharmacists -> 0..Stock]
    /\ shift \in [Pharmacists -> {"idle", "preparing", "down"}]
===========================================================================

CONSTANT Pharmacists = {ph1, ph2}
CONSTANT Stock = 3
CONSTANT MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FreshSnapshotAgrees
INVARIANT StockLedger
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
A pharmacy's prescription dispenser keeps one shared stock ledger for a controlled medication, protected by optimistic locking rather than locks. A pharmacist who wants to dispense first reads the ledger, taking a snapshot of both the current stock level and the ledger's version number. She then prepares the dispense off to the side; when ready she commits, but the commit is accepted only if the ledger's version still equals the version she read. Every accepted commit removes one unit from stock, bumps the version, and counts one completed dispense, which silently invalidates every other pharmacist's outstanding snapshot. A pharmacist whose snapshot has gone stale simply abandons her attempt and retries with a fresh read. Any pharmacist can also crash silently mid-transaction, leaving her snapshot dangling until she is brought back on shift and starts over. Initially the ledger is at version zero with full stock and every pharmacist idle.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a pharmacist's snapshot version still matches the live ledger version, her snapshotted stock level equals the live stock level, so no committed update can ever be silently lost.

A hospital operating-room scheduler hands out its OR slots to surgical teams as leases that expire after a fixed number of clock ticks. A team leases a free slot, becoming scheduled for it, and the slot's countdown starts from the full lease duration. The ward clock ticks slot countdowns toward zero, and when a countdown reaches zero on a leased slot whose team has not yet begun operating, the scheduler reclaims the slot; the team may be slow but has not failed, so it can still believe it holds the slot. Such a slow team must discover its lease is gone and stand down without entering the OR. A team actually begins operating only after re-validating that the lease table still names it for the slot, and each operation consumes one sterile instrument kit from a shared store. When surgery finishes the team logs a completed case, releases the slot, and rests. The scheduler never reclaims a slot while its team is in the middle of an operation. Initially all slots are free, all teams are resting, and the kit store is full.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no operating room slot is ever allocated to two teams at once, and any team actually operating in a slot is the single team the lease table names for it.

A container-ship crane yard has one shared transfer bridge that the quay cranes must use to move containers off the import stack. Before a crane mounts the bridge, the yard's duty controllers vote; the crane needs a strict majority of the controllers currently on duty. Controllers go on and off duty at runtime, so the size of the electorate and therefore the quorum threshold changes while votes are being gathered. When a crane wins its majority and the bridge is clear, it mounts the bridge, pulls one container off the stack, and all ballots are wiped for the next round. SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one crane is ever mounted on the shared transfer bridge, and every crane that is mid-hoist is exactly the crane the bridge records as mounted.

A hospital operating-room scheduler takes surgery requests through a bounded intake queue and applies them to a shared day roster. Booking clerks add requests to the queue only while it has room; when it is full the ward exerts backpressure and clerks must wait. The queue's capacity itself changes at runtime: an administrator can widen it, or narrow it down to no less than its current occupancy. Two scheduler workers pull requests off the queue; a worker stages a request together with a snapshot of the roster's current booking count. To book, a staged worker re-checks that its snapshot still matches the live roster and that an unallocated theatre hour remains, then writes the incremented roster and consumes that hour. If another worker has changed the roster in between, the stale worker re-reads a fresh snapshot rather than overwriting blindly, and a staged request can also be abandoned when a patient cancels. Every booking that reaches the roster therefore consumes exactly one theatre hour, so the roster and the remaining hours always reconcile. The day begins with an empty queue, all theatre hours free, an untouched roster, and both workers idle.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared day roster never loses an update, so the booking count always equals exactly the number of theatre hours consumed.

An air-traffic runway allocator manages a fixed fleet of aircraft cycling between a holding pattern, the final approach, and the apron after landing. Before any aircraft may leave the holding pattern for final approach, the tower's controllers vote on the clearance, and the allocator acts only when a strict majority of the full controller bench backs the same clearance. A controller can crash silently at any moment: it simply stops voting, still counts in the majority denominator, and gives no sign of failure, so clearances become harder to win but never unsafe. Crashed controllers may later be rebooted, returning with their ballots wiped. When a clearance wins its majority, one aircraft moves from holding onto final approach and all ballots are cleared for the next round. An aircraft on final approach eventually touches down and joins the apron count, and parked aircraft later depart, re-entering the holding pattern. Aircraft are never created or destroyed: every plane in the fleet is always in exactly one of the three stages. The day starts with the whole fleet in holding, no votes cast, and every controller alive.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the aircraft in holding, on final approach, and parked on the apron always sum to exactly the fixed fleet size, with no aircraft created or destroyed.

A multiplayer game lobby seats players through a matchmaker whose only shared state is a compare-and-swap register holding the current seat count. Each matchmaker thread reads the register to arm itself with an expected value, then attempts to seat a player by swapping in the incremented count; the swap succeeds only if the register still equals the thread's expected value. A successful seat also draws one entry ticket from the lobby's ticket roll, so seats and remaining tickets must always reconcile exactly. If another thread has won the race in between, the stale thread's swap fails and it goes back to re-read. The lobby's capacity is not fixed: an operator can grow it mid-session or shrink it down to no less than the players already seated, and no swap may ever push the count past the current capacity. Players also leave the lobby at will, freeing a seat and returning their ticket to the roll. The session opens with an empty register, a full ticket roll, both threads idle, and capacity at its starting value.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no update to the seat register is ever lost, so the tickets remaining on the roll always equal exactly the roll's full size minus the players currently seated.

An air-traffic runway allocator assigns arriving flights to runways using a lock-free scheme built around a compare-and-swap generation register. An allocator thread first snapshots the generation number, chooses a runway that is currently open and unoccupied, and then attempts the assignment; the assignment takes effect only if the generation register still equals the snapshot, in which case the register advances by one and a landing clearance is consumed from the tower's fixed book of clearances. The field never allows a flight onto a closed runway, so occupancy can never exceed what the open runways provide. Initially the register is at zero, all runways are open and empty, both threads are resting, and the clearance book is full.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the set of occupied runways never exceeds the currently open runways, so flights only ever sit on runways that operations has open.

nl:
A smart-home door lock network guards the front door with a credential register that works like a compare-and-swap cell: a phone may throw the bolt only by presenting a credential whose generation exactly matches the generation currently stored in the lock. Family phones sync themselves with the hub to pick up the current generation, but a phone can be arbitrarily slow between syncing and actually trying the door: it has not failed, it is just late, and by then the hub may have rotated the keys. The hub rotates the credential generation whenever the door is bolted, cycling through its generation space, and every rotation instantly makes all previously synced credentials stale. A stale phone's unlock attempt is refused by the mismatch, and the phone must sync again. A successful unlock records which phone opened the door and drains one unit from the lock's battery pack, and the hub never rotates keys while the door stands open. Anyone inside can bolt the door again, clearing the opener record. The house starts bolted, every phone freshly synced, the battery full, and no unlocks on the log.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the door is never opened by an unauthorized or stale device: whenever the door stands open, the phone recorded as the opener holds a credential matching the lock's current generation.

IdleStamp == MaxVer + 1

Init ==
    /\ tab = [w \in Windows |-> OPEN]
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ armedAt = [b \in Banks |-> IdleStamp]
    /\ book = [b \in Banks |-> {}]
    /\ settled = 0
    /\ reserve = Reserve

ArmClaim(b) ==
    /\ armedAt[b] = IdleStamp
    /\ armedAt' = [armedAt EXCEPT ![b] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tab, ver, book, settled, reserve>>

SubmitClaim(b, w) ==
    /\ armedAt[b] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ tab[w] = OPEN
    /\ tab' = [tab EXCEPT ![w] = b]
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![b] = book[b] \cup {w}]
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ armedAt' = [armedAt EXCEPT ![b] = IdleStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<settled, reserve>>

RefusedStale(b) ==
    /\ armedAt[b] /= IdleStamp
    /\ armedAt[b] /= ver
    /\ armedAt' = [armedAt EXCEPT ![b] = IdleStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tab, ver, book, settled, reserve>>

WalkAway(b) ==
    /\ armedAt[b] /= IdleStamp
    /\ armedAt' = [armedAt EXCEPT ![b] = IdleStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tab, ver, book, settled, reserve>>

SettleWindow(b, w) ==
    /\ w \in book[b]
    /\ reserve > 0
    /\ settled' = 1 + settled
    /\ reserve' = reserve - 1
    /\ tab' = [tab EXCEPT ![w] = OPEN]
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![b] = book[b] \ {w}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, armedAt>>

UnwindClaim(b, w) ==
    /\ w \in book[b]
    /\ tab' = [tab EXCEPT ![w] = OPEN]
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![b] = book[b] \ {w}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, armedAt, settled, reserve>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : ArmClaim(b) \/ RefusedStale(b) \/ WalkAway(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks, w \in Windows :

nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch clears through a set of numbered clearing windows that member banks claim optimistically, without any lock. A bank first arms itself by reading the claims table's version stamp. To claim a window it submits the claim along with its remembered stamp; the operator accepts only if the table's version is still the one the bank read and the window is still open, then records the bank as the window's owner, adds the window to that bank's book, and bumps the version. A bank can be slow without having failed: it may sit armed for a long while, and if rival claims have bumped the version in the meantime its submission is refused as stale and it must re-arm; it can also simply walk away from an armed attempt. Settling an owned window pays out one unit of the batch's liquidity reserve, clears the owner from the table, and tallies one settled window, so the tally and the remaining reserve always reconcile. The operator may also unwind an owned claim administratively, reopening the window without paying anything. No clearing window may ever appear in two banks' books, and every window in a bank's book must be exactly the one the claims table says it owns. The batch opens with every window open, both banks idle, an untouched reserve, and version zero.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no clearing window is ever double-allocated: every window recorded in a bank's book is owned by that bank alone in the claims table.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m3p5t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, Flights, Carts, MaxTerm, LEADERLESS

VARIABLES term, chief, nodeTerm, released, dispatched, carts

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ chief = LEADERLESS
    /\ nodeTerm = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ released = [f \in Flights |-> 0]
    /\ dispatched = 0
    /\ carts = Carts

ElectChief(n) ==
    /\ chief = LEADERLESS
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ chief' = n
    /\ nodeTerm' = [nodeTerm EXCEPT ![n] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<released, dispatched, carts>>

DeposeChief ==
    /\ chief /= LEADERLESS
    /\ chief' = LEADERLESS
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, nodeTerm, released, dispatched, carts>>

ReleaseBags(n, f) ==
    /\ chief = n
    /\ nodeTerm[n] = term
    /\ released[f] = 0
    /\ carts > 0
    /\ released' = [released EXCEPT ![f] = released[f] + 1]
    /\ dispatched' = 1 + dispatched
    /\ carts' = carts - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, nodeTerm>>

LearnTerm(n) ==
    /\ nodeTerm[n] < term
    /\ nodeTerm' = [nodeTerm EXCEPT ![n] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, released, dispatched, carts>>

StandbyPing ==
    /\ chief = LEADERLESS
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, nodeTerm, released, dispatched, carts>>

Next ==
    \/ DeposeChief \/ StandbyPing
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : ElectChief(n) \/ LearnTerm(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, f \in Flights : ReleaseBags(n, f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReleaseAtMostOnce == \A f \in Flights : released[f] <= 1
CartLedger == dispatched = Carts - carts

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ chief \in Nodes \cup {LEADERLESS}
    /\ nodeTerm \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ released \in [Flights -> 0..2]
    /\ dispatched \in 0..Carts
    /\ carts \in 0..Carts
===========================================================================

CONSTANT Nodes = {rtr1, rtr2}
CONSTANT Flights = {fl1, fl2}
CONSTANT Carts = 2
CONSTANT MaxTerm = 3
CONSTANT LEADERLESS = LEADERLESS
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ReleaseAtMostOnce
INVARIANT CartLedger
INVARIANT TypeOK
nl:
An airport baggage router puts one of its two router nodes in charge through leader election with failover. Electing a node advances the election term, and the winner records the new term as its own; the operations desk can depose a leader it suspects of being slow, leaving the system leaderless until the next election. A deposed node may only be slow rather than failed: it can wake up much later still believing it leads under its old term, so every privileged action is checked against the current term and current leadership. The privileged action is irreversible: releasing a flight's bags onto the aircraft loader, which can never be recalled and must happen at most once per flight. A release requires the acting node to be the current leader on the current term, the flight to be unreleased, and it consumes one baggage cart from the cart pool while tallying one dispatched release. Nodes that fell behind can re-learn the current term from the election board. While the system is leaderless the standby nodes merely ping the board, changing nothing. The morning starts leaderless at term zero, all flights unreleased, the cart pool full, and no releases tallied.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible bag release happens at most once per flight: no flight's release record ever exceeds a single dispatch.
